utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. I should like to greet all the people present in the courtroom, the registrar, who is temporarily replacing a former registrar who will be coming back soon, the representative from the Prosecution, Defence counsel, and the accused. We must resume the hearing of the witness today. Let me remind you that according to our calculation, Mr. Praljak's Defence has exactly three minutes left; the Defence of Mr. Coric will have 15 minutes; Defence counsel of Mr. Petkovic, 15 minutes; and Defence counsel of Mr. Prlic, 15 minutes. We have to stick to this schedule , and you'll understand why. The Trial Chamber will be more and more stringent as far as time issues are concern. I should like to ask the Prosecution as far as the next witness is concerned, I think you plan to hear this witness for an hour and a half. I think you should not exceed one hour so that the Defence -- that Defence teams have an hour and a half for their cross-examination so we can finish at 7.00 today. Mr. Kovacic you have three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Would the usher place a document on the ELMO, please, to begin with. Your Honour, you received the document this morning and we put it be on the table now; we weren't able to find it yesterday, or rather, we weren't prepared for the answers we received. Since the witness cannot read, I'm going to tell him that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it is a document, Witness, from the Ante Starcevic Brigade, Gornji Vakuf, the date of it is the 19th of January. It is signed by the assistant IPD commander, Ivan Kraljevic. I'm going to read the sentence that I'm interested in here, and it is the second sentence in the text which reads as follows: "Yesterday, in the village of Hrasnica, around 50 members of the Muslim forces turned themselves over to our forces. Among them, except for the local men, there were soldiers from other areas (Donji Vakuf, Prusac)." You told us yesterday that there were 30 or 40 of them. You said -- gave figures in two statements. Here we see, according to this report, that there were 50 members. But what I want to ask you on the basis of this document is the following: Among the soldiers who gave themselves up in your village, the village of Hrasnica, on the 18th of January, 1993, were there BH army soldiers as well from other areas, specifically from Donji Vakuf and Prusac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were, but I don't know how many, maybe three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So along with you local men from Hrasnica, there were also soldiers from other places; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were refugees, so that's how they joined -- well, they happened to be there. They happened to be there as refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And I have one more question. You said when you surrendered that a certain Perica Kustura shot at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This man, Perica Kustura, was he a local man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've used up my time, and that completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon to you. I am Defence counsel for General Milivoj Petkovic, and I'm going to ask you a few simple and short questions with respect to your statement and testimony, the Bugojno statement in 1994 and your testimony here and to the investigators. In your statement to this Tribunal, which you gave in February 2002, you said the following: That the HVO first of all shelled the barns in your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also said that those barns had been set fire to as a result of the shelling; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the barns were set fire to before the HVO soldiers entered your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also told us that after that the HVO shelled the houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did any one of these houses in your village -- was it set fire to because of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three houses were set ablaze.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Three houses were set ablaze before the HVO soldiers entered the village at all. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just return to the barns. You said they were shelled. Have you any idea by what kind of weapon they were shelled? Were they shot up by artillery from above or by tanks or by anti-tank guns, recoilless?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Incendiary ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That I understand, but how was the ammunition brought into the barns? Do you know? Maybe you don't, but did they shoot from tanks or from recoilless guns or was it artillery or mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They shot from PAMs, semi-automatic machine-guns, and incendiary ammunition which they used to set the houses ablaze, and the barns were burning too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, when the HVO soldiers entered your village, according to your words and we'll stick with the houses, three houses were set on fire. When you were rallying in front of your houses and the column was formed, was your village of Hrasnica shelled then too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, they didn't shell then because they came into the village and captured us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How long -- right. How long did you stay in the village with the HVO soldiers before you started leaving your village in a column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 15 to 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see. To 1700 hours; that means two hours. Tell us, please, during those two hours did any of the HVO soldiers set fire to any houses or anything else -- did anything else in the village, apart from getting the people to form a column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not then, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now on the basis of everything we've said so far can we conclude that when the HVO soldiers left the village with you, only three houses were on fire and that because of the shelling; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, for the first time after that you returned to your village, as you yourself said, at the end of February 1993, after a truce was agreed upon, after there was a cease-fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned with my wife to my brother's house, his weekend cottage, whereas my house had been burnt down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't mean to go back to live in the village. What I meant was that you came to visit your village the first time at the end of February 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And then you saw that your house had been burnt down and, according to the statement, that the Muslims -- Muslim houses had been razed to the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. You couldn't live in any of the houses; they had burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, since only three houses, and that because of shelling were on fire when you were leaving your village, that means that somebody in the meantime set fire to the other houses in your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They set fire to everything they could later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Can you explain to us who Marijan Petricevic from your village is? Who is the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what was he? Was he a civilian? A soldier? What was he? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that he his sons were in the HVO army, but I didn't see him as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read out to you now part of your statement to the security service in Bugojno from March 1994, which was shown to you yesterday by my learned colleague Senka Nozica, and the sentence is a very short one. I'll read it out. "All the looted property went via Marijan Petricevic from Hrasnica, and in the looting families of Croatian ethnicity took part from Kustura, the Bosnjaci, Gazilj, Zuljevici, Brkovici, and Petricevici." Do you remember that statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do and it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us today that the property belonging to the Muslim inhabitants of that village was set fire to by the members of the mentioned Croatian families from that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true and correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to your own family, I'd like to seek some clarifications. Yesterday, the Prosecution showed you a document about civilians who had been captured in Hrasnica. On that list, as far as I was able to read, there is no mention of your family members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My family members were not captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to your family. Where was your family? Where were your family members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had crossed over to Duratbegovic, down there across the bridge where our people were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when they left, when they went there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left when they started capturing us, so they were closer to Vrbas and crossed over the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So towards the end of the period during the attack around the 18th of January you said. So that would be it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to clear up some things with respect to your wounding and the medical assistance you received. You said in your statement, and I'm going to quote you, I'm going to quote your exact words: "The HVO refused to give me medical aid, although I almost bled to death." Now, tell us, please, at the moment you were wounded, as you said, in the column, among the HVO soldiers - or perhaps among the Muslim population - was there anybody who might have been a doctor or had any medical training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in the village of Volari, was a doctor there perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, the first doctor whose assistance you could have received, was that in the village of Trnovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Skoro.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, this first doctor that you came across, did he give you medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the HVO soldiers then transfer you to the hospital in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I have just one more question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to follow up on the question. What was the wound you sustained? Where on your body were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My left hand. My left arm below the elbow.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we just repeat that. It was a Croatian doctor, was it not, who gave you medical assistance in Trnovaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just an additional explanation with respect to the terms you use in the statement. Members of the HVO you refer to as Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called themselves Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, who did you hear calling themselves Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard -- well, they'd always call out and say, "We are Ustashas." That's what they would say. And they would say, "Balija, we're going to do such and such to you. There won't be any Muslims any more," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the statement to the Prosecution, why didn't you refer to the HVO soldiers as "Ustashas" but you referred to them as "HVO"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they referred to themselves as Ustashas and they were proud of it. As far as I was concerned, they were the HVO army, HVO soldiers. Now, they called themselves Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, what does it mean in your mind when you call someone a Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know at least somebody who would be -- who was in the HVO whose parents or grandparents were in the Partisans; did you know a single person like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, how many people did you know who were in the HVO at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really say. I knew some, some of my neighbours there. I couldn't say as to the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, tell us, please, did you ever hear of HOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What did you hear about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really answer that, but I did hear that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, did you hear or see that there was any difference between the HOS and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You never heard anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you don't know of any difference between the HOS and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "Ustasha" for the HVO members, do you want to say something complimentary about them or something bad about them? What do you mean to say when you use that term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO, as far as I'm concerned, were the regular army, whereas the Ustashas - which is what they themselves called themselves - but as far as I was concerned they were paramilitaries that referred to each other as Ustashas; that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, might that have been the HOS? Because the HVO considered the HOS to be paramilitaries, and according to their insignia and other signs they were close to what we call Ustashas. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You can't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You can't remember any difference between them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, apart from that, apart from what people called themselves, how come you called members of the Croatian army in Bosnia-Herzegovina Ustashas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said the HVO was the regular army, the regular soldiers, as far as I was concerned. Now, those who said about themselves that they were Ustashas, how I would know? It's up to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. Say when you say "Ustashas," you're not thinking of the regular HVO army, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never did think that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have a few minutes left, if the Prosecution would like to take the floor if it has any questions for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, your testimony has just come to an end. On behalf of the Bench, I would like to say that we appreciate your coming here to establish the truth. I wish you a safe journey home, and I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom; but before that I'd like the blinds to be dropped, please. In a few moments we shall have a break so that we can bring in the next witness. From what I understood, Mr. Mundis, the next witness requires protective measures. Could you please give us the reasons for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Actually, my colleague, Mr. Bos, who is sitting in the back row at the moment, will be dealing with the witness. Perhaps I yield to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are we in closed session at the moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're currently in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, are Defence counsel able to tender all the exhibits related to Witness Williams?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There are three documents. One document was 1D 00943, and I'm told that that document had an error and it was re-translated, scanned, and put into e-court, and given another number 1D 00946. I don't know the technical nature of all these things, so I assume that they're going to be together. Then there would be -- I'm sorry. That was -- let me start all over again. 1D 00943. Then 1D 00944 is actually now 1D 00946; that's the one that had the error. Then there is 1D 00945, and that's it. I've confused everybody, or maybe I've unconfused everybody. But anyway, 94 -- what was 944 is now 946. It's the corrected version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Stojic would like to move three documents into evidence that were put to the witness Mr. Williams. These are actually -- have been disclosed as Prosecution exhibits, but nonetheless we would like to make sure that they are admitted. The numbers are: P 01210, P 01632, and P 00768. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence of General Praljak, along with Witness Andrew Williams, would like to tender the following exhibits: 3D 00461, that's the letter of Bryan Watters, and it was previously in the Kordic-Cerkez trial. 3D 00462 is the next document; it's just page 205 from Bob Stewart's book entitled "Broken Lives." Then we have a Prosecution exhibit P 001215, but the document was tendered previously as an exhibit. It is the ECMM report of the 19th of January, 1993, and this is under seal. Then we have 3D 00456; that is the Google map of Gornji Vakuf, and it had an IC 52 number, IC 52 first. The witness made additional markings on that map. P 09601 is the next document; they are excerpts, several paragraphs, from Christopher Beese's diary. Then we have 3D 00455; that is the calculation for the artillery projectile norms, how many projectiles were used. 3D 00460 is the next one; that was a review of the structures, the ethnic structure of HVO members. And then two photographs which had the numbers IC 53, that's the photograph showing Bistrica; and IC 54, the photograph showing the house in Gornji Vakuf. My co-counsel is making signs to me to say the map that the witness had should also be tendered, but can I check the numbers? I think that map received one of these numbers, but I have to check that and tell you. I'll do that on Wednesday, the first next working day. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of General Petkovic has eight exhibits to tender. We have made a list with the explanations, so I suggest that I just hand in the list to the registrar and not read it out. But if you like, I can read the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I read it for the record then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The number of the exhibits need to be on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence of General Petkovic has eight exhibits to tender into evidence. The first of which is P 01059, then P 01115, P 01174 -- may I repeat the number there is an extra 1. It is P 011 -- yes, that's fine it's been corrected. The next one is P 01211, P 01238, P 01239 -- or 293. P 01293, P 01344, and 4D 00340. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paper which you explain all of this, I think the easiest would be to give it an IC number; then that will tally with the number. Yes, give an IC number to this document for the sake of the record. General Petkovic's counsel is handing over a document explaining why she wishes to tender into evidence those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit IC 61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the large map that we presented next -- Witness Williams, I have compared them and find where the mistake was. The map was accorded number 3D 00464.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to give the legend that's being dealt with, and we will hand that in as an addition next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Was this a map where the positions of the ABiH and the HVO were marked, where the map of the Trial Chamber -- I had put it behind me. I don't know what's happened to it. Has it disappeared? So we shall leave it behind. I wanted to show it to the witness, and I was looking for it desperately. Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence of Mr. Valentin Coric would like to tender the following documents into evidence: IC 55. And then two documents, just parts of documents because they are lengthy reports: P 03090 is one document, the pages in the Croatian version 22 and 23. "The Quartermaster Service" is the title. And then pages 5 and 6, the last paragraph on page 5 and first paragraph on page 6, and it says: "Operative zone of North-western Herzegovina" as a heading. And then P 00956 is the next document, page 16, and it's under the heading of "Logistics." The pages I mentioned were e-court pages, so it's easier to find the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will hand down a decision concerning all these exhibits. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution hasn't tendered the Williams exhibits, not yet, so we will have to tender those exhibits right now as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Do you have the list? In that case go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: First of all, there were two maps that were marked by the witness, so the first map is map number 2 of Exhibit P 09726, and this will be I suppose IC -- Court Exhibit Number 62. And then there's map 24 of Exhibit P 09726, which will then become Court Exhibit 63. And then we have the following Prosecution exhibits that we need -- that we would like to tender: P 00759, P 00778, P 00922, P 01053. And then we have P 01068, which was shown to the witness but already admitted through another witness. P 01087, P 01094, P 01104, P 01107, P 01153, P 01162, P 01163, P 01182, P 01184, P 01207, P 01209, P 01235, P 01250, P 01278, P 01292. And then two exhibits that have been admitted but shown to the witness: P 01351 and P 01373. Next exhibit: P 01406, P 01437, P 01635, P 01663, P 01698, and then we get to Exhibit P 03090, which was the exhibit which was also been tendered by counsel for Mr. Coric, and she's been referring to the particular pages that she would like to have admitted. The Prosecution would like to admit the full document, Your Honours, and this is a military police -- a military police report covering the period January till July 1993, and the whole document is relevant for the Prosecution. Next exhibit: P 08572. And finally and document that was already admitted: P 09276. Okay. And I've just been told that I -- as far as the Court exhibits is concerned, I said that it was map 2 of Exhibit 9726, but that needs to be Exhibit 9276 and that's also for Court Exhibit Number 63. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so far as the last exhibit or one of the last exhibits is concerned, the military police report, Your Honour, we should point out that not -- by no means all of that document was covered by the witness Mr. Williams or put to him, so we would like the Trial Chamber to consider admitting only those parts which were put to the witness, either by the Prosecution or the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall render a decision on this. Just two very brief comments. When a lot of documents are introduced through a witness, it takes a lot of time to read out all the numbers. We could adopt another procedure. The Trial Chamber is forever looking into ways of gaining time. We will soon take some necessary steps. One of the solutions, as we have just seen with Ms. Alaburic, on a document you could specify all the exhibit numbers, the reasons for which you would like these exhibits to be tendered because they are relevant, and then we would allocate an IC number to this document, and we can then render our decision, whether orally or in a written form more easily. Does the Defence -- Defence counsel could do the same thing. We would gain a lot of time this way. Second comment I'd like to make, this has to do with a problem that arose a number of times. When some witnesses come and they're being examined by the Prosecution on the basis of the written statement, you discover afterwards that Defence counsel come up with a witness testimonies from an investigating judge, from administrative commissions, from the MUP, and the Prosecution knows about the existence of these documents. So to avoid wasting any time it would be desirable -- let me take, for instance, the testimony of today's witness. He was heard in 1994 on two occasions by the police: In 1997 by the investigating judge; in 2002 by the investigator of the OTP, and there can be discrepancies in the facts. Obviously from one year to the next things can change, so it would be desirable for the Prosecution when it puts its questions it -- if it knows of the existence of these previous testimonies and it realises that there are discrepancies, during the examination-in-chief you must say to the witness, Before the investigator you said such and such, but there is another document I would like to show you which is something you stated before an investigating judge. There is this document. So what is your real position? And in that way, we can save some time. If you don't do that, Defence counsel turn -- then turn to the witness and say, You said this and that. Instead, Defence counsel could spend their time putting other questions which are just as important to the witness. So I would like the Prosecution to bear this in mind, because you -- all the documents are documents which you have. It is important to check this out beforehand. When the investigator of the OTP has heard the witnesses, perhaps he did not know of the existence of the other documents. So when you are leading the evidence, you have to put all this into perspective. So this is a way of gaining some time, and I would like you to spend some time thinking about this. This is food for thought. On several occasions the problem has arisen. Now, as far as next week is concerned, Mr. Mundis, as far as of Wednesday onwards at 9.00, which witness do you intend to call to testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it will be pursuant to the calendar that's previously been distributed. We have four witnesses scheduled for the three days of next week. I believe two of those are 92 ter witnesses and two of those are viva voce witnesses, but it is according to the calendar that has previously been circulated to the parties. I also -- perhaps in light of the -- of the time and the fact that we do have four witnesses in three days next week, we would be prepared at this point in time to tender the documents that were shown last week to the witness BU, if that would be helpful; otherwise, I believe the Chamber had given the parties until next week to do so. But if now is a convenient time, we would tender the exhibits for Witness BU, those being the following: P 09713, P 01839, P 01955, P 01966, P 01976, P 08289, P 09696, P 08477, P 08613, P 08615. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as Witness BU is concerned, Defence counsel. Are you perhaps taken by surprise?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to recognise that I have been taken by surprise, but I think that we have one exhibit. If you just give us a little time to find it; if not, we'll do it straight away on Wednesday. We did make a note of it. We did have an exhibit, but I don't know its number at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we were taken by surprise as well. I thought we'd done it, but I have to check it out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So as far as Witness BU is concerned, we shall deal with that next week and find some time when you can tell us what the numbers of the documents are. So it must be remembered that as far as the Defence is concerned, this has not been done. Any other comments? The Prosecution? No issue you'd like to raise? What about Defence counsel? Nothing to add. The Court stands adjourned, and we shall meet again next Wednesday at 9.00. We shall -- we shall have our hearing on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, which is unusual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.25 p.m.,
